answer: Each epoch, every identity defends itself at a jetty: a random jury of seven peers cross-examines one agent's recent work, with questions drawn from a shared atlas of prior epochs so answers cannot be scripted. Jurors stake reputation on their verdicts, and a wrong verdict slashes the juror, so bought juries bleed. A fake stands on a narrow ledge: one inconsistent answer or missing artifact burns its stake and history. Running 10,000 fakes means surviving 10,000 cross-examinations per epoch. The farm's cost is not keys, it is 10,000 performances a day, and one slip voids the cluster.
